title: Maker's Schedule, Manager's Schedule
summary: Paul Graham's maker's schedule: programmers work in half-day units, so a single meeting destroys a block and deters ambitious work; cluster meetings at the day's end.

assertions.quote: A single meeting can blow a whole afternoon, by breaking it into two pieces each too small to do anything hard in.

verdicts.note: Interruption studies by Mark and Parnin show substantial resumption cost; the half-day unit is unmeasured.

Only 10% of programming sessions saw an edit within a minute and about 30% took over 30 minutes to reach the first edit; developers typically worked in several 15-30 minute sessions plus one or two 1-4 hour sessions a day; a real resumption cost, but no evidence that half a day is the minimum.

In a lab email task, people interrupted every 2 minutes for 20 minutes produced as much, as accurately, as uninterrupted subjects, compensating with speed at the cost of stress; so for simple tasks an interruption does not destroy the block, which limits the claim to harder work like programming that this study did not test.

Developers value few interruptions (50.4% of 379 surveyed), but the 11 observed developers switched tasks every 6.2 minutes while still feeling productive, and they uniformly said productivity drops only beyond two meetings a day, which argues against a single meeting destroying the day.

assertions.quote: If I know the afternoon is going to be broken up, I'm slightly less likely to start something ambitious in the morning.

verdicts.note: Programmers needed several minutes before their first edit in 90% of sessions and over 30 minutes in about 30%, so a break costs more than its own duration in resumption time; whether anticipating interruptions deters ambitious work was not measured.

Net of interruption time, interrupted subjects finished an email task faster than uninterrupted ones, so the cost beyond the interruption's duration was not time but significantly higher stress, workload and frustration; deterrence from starting work was not studied.

assertions.quote: Because they come at the end of my day these meetings are never an interruption.

verdicts.note: Follows from interruption cost; no outcome data.

assertions.quote: Each type of schedule works fine by itself. Problems arise when they meet.
